response.justification: Bogdan is an experienced, versatile senior engineer with genuine geospatial credentials (GISCollective, Green Map web GIS, FOSS4G talk) and relevant low-latency, high-throughput distributed systems work at Sociomantic/Dunnhumby using async I/O, fibers, and caching at millions of requests per second. However, the role's core requirement — modern C++ (or Rust) in commercial or open-source settings — is only weakly met: his C/C++ exposure is limited to roughly seven months at National Instruments in 2014-2015 and a university thesis, with no Rust at all. His systems depth is largely in D, which is conceptually adjacent but not what the team hires for, and the last five years have been TypeScript/Node/AWS product work. There is also no navigation guidance, routing, or map-tiling pipeline experience. Worth a screening call if the team will accept a strong systems generalist willing to ramp on C++, but he is not a direct-hit candidate.
strengths: Real geospatial/GIS product experience, including an open-source map data platform
Proven low-latency, high-throughput microservice work at massive request volumes
Strong engineering discipline: TDD, CI/CD, own testing tooling, Linux and DevOps depth
concerns: Minimal modern C++ (~7 months, 2014) and no Rust experience
No navigation, routing, or map-tiling pipeline background
Recent 5+ years focused on TypeScript/Node web stacks, not systems programming
